request.query: Cardinality of a subset of a finite Cartesian product is at most product of cardinalities of coordinate sets

items.type: ∀ {M : Type u_2} [inst : Mul M] {s t : Set M}, Cardinal.mk ↑(s * t) ≤ Cardinal.mk ↑s * Cardinal.mk ↑t
items.informal_description: For any subsets $s$ and $t$ of a type $\alpha$ equipped with a multiplication operation, the cardinality of the product set $s \cdot t$ is less than or equal to the product of the cardinalities of $s$ and $t$. Symbolically, $|s \cdot t| \leq |s| \cdot |t|$.

items.type: ∀ {α : Type u_2} [inst : DecidableEq α] [inst_1 : Mul α] {s t : Finset α}, (s * t).card ≤ s.card * t.card
items.informal_description: For any finite sets $ s $ and $ t $, the cardinality of their pointwise product $ s \cdot t $ satisfies $ \#(s \cdot t) \leq \#s \cdot \#t $. This inequality holds because the product set $ s \cdot t $ contains at most $ \#s \cdot \#t $ distinct elements, accounting for possible overlaps in the products of elements from $ s $ and $ t $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Binary Image ≤ Product of Set Sizes
items.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {β : Type u_3} {γ : Type u_5} [inst : DecidableEq γ] (f : α → β → γ) (s : Finset α) (t : Finset β),
  (Finset.image₂ f s t).card ≤ s.card * t.card
items.informal_description: For any binary function $ f : \alpha \to \beta \to \gamma $ and finite sets $ s \subseteq \alpha $ and $ t \subseteq \beta $, the cardinality of the image of $ f $ on $ s \times t $ is less than or equal to the product of the cardinalities of $ s $ and $ t $, i.e., $ \#(\mathrm{image}_2\, f\, s\, t) \leq \#s \cdot \#t $.

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Dependent Product of Finite Sets: $ |s.\pi t| = \prod_{i \in s} |t(i)| $
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_4} {α : ι → Type u_6} [inst : DecidableEq ι] (s : Finset ι) (t : (i : ι) → Finset (α i)),
  (s.pi t).card = ∏ i ∈ s, (t i).card
items.informal_description: For a finite set $ s $ over a type $ \iota $ and a function $ t $ assigning to each $ i \in s $ a finite set $ t(i) $, the cardinality of the set of all functions $ f $ such that $ f(i) \in t(i) $ for each $ i \in s $ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of each $ t(i) $, i.e., $ |s.\pi t| = \prod_{i \in s} |t(i)| $.

items.informal_description: For any two subsets $ s $ and $ t $ of a type $ \alpha $ with a multiplication operation, the cardinality of their product set $ s \cdot t $ satisfies $ |s \cdot t| \leq |s| \cdot |t| $, where $ |\cdot| $ denotes the natural number cardinality (with infinite sets mapped to zero).

items.informal_name: Cardinality of Dependent Product of Finite Sets Over a Finite Type
items.type:
∀ {ι : Type u_4} {α : ι → Type u_6} [inst : DecidableEq ι] [inst_1 : Fintype ι] (s : (i : ι) → Finset (α i)),
  (Fintype.piFinset s).card = ∏ i, (s i).card
items.informal_description: Given a finite type $\alpha$ and a family of finite sets $s(i)$ indexed by $\alpha$, the cardinality of the set of all functions $f : \alpha \to \bigcup_i \delta(i)$ satisfying $f(i) \in s(i)$ for every $i \in \alpha$ is equal to the product of the cardinalities of each $s(i)$. In symbols, $\#(\pi\text{Finset}\, s) = \prod_{i} \#(s(i))$.
